title: Probing the Prefill: Detecting Code Vulnerabilities via Latent Activations
abstract: arXiv:2608.16970v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM-based code generation is now embedded in mission-critical pipelines, but defenses against vulnerable output remain post-hoc -- static analyzers, fine-tuned classifiers, or an LLM judge that screen completed code, ignoring the generating model's own internal state. We test a narrower, directly measurable question: when an LLM reads a piece of C/C++ code as context, do its hidden activations already carry a signal about that code's vulnerability status? We extract last prefill token activations from four LLMs (Granite-4.1-8B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.6-27B, Gemma-4-12B) across three model families and train MLP probes on these activations. We evaluate them on four function-level C/C++ benchmarks (Devign, Big-Vul, Draper VDISC, PrimeVul). Our probes achieve 41.7\% average F1 using 13.4--16.0M-parameter probes -- under 0.2\% of base-model size. On Devign, the best probe (Qwen3.5-9B, 68.8\% F1) matches the published fine-tuned-classifier SOTA

translated_title: 探测预填充阶段：通过潜在激活检测代码漏洞
translated_abstract: 基于LLM的代码生成现已嵌入关键任务流程中，但针对易受攻击输出的防御仍然是事后性的——静态分析器、微调分类器或LLM审查器会筛选已完成的代码，而忽略了生成模型自身的内部状态。我们测试了一个更窄、可直接度量的问题：当LLM将一段C/C++代码作为上下文读取时，其隐藏激活是否已经携带了关于该代码漏洞状态的信号？我们从三个模型家族的四款LLM（Granite-4.1-8B、Qwen3.5-9B、Qwen3.6-27B、Gemma-4-12B）中提取最后一个预填充令牌的激活，并基于这些激活训练MLP探针。我们在四个函数级C/C++基准测试（Devign、Big-Vul、Draper VDISC、PrimeVul）上进行了评估。我们的探针使用13.4至16.0M参数的探针实现了41.7%的平均F1分数——不到基础模型规模的0.2%。在Devign上，最佳探针（Qwen3.5-9B，68.8%的F1分数）与已发表的微调分类器SOTA持平。
tldr: 本研究首次证明，仅通过LLM预填充阶段最后令牌的隐藏激活，轻量级MLP探针即可有效检测C/C++代码漏洞，以不到0.2%的模型参数规模达到与微调分类器SOTA相当的性能。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates for the first time that lightweight MLP probes trained on the last prefill token's latent activations can effectively detect C/C++ code vulnerabilities, achieving performance comparable to fine-tuned classifier SOTA with less than 0.2% of the base model's parameters.
